clusters.label: Exchange current density
clusters.definition: Current density characterizing equilibrium redox exchange kinetics.
clusters.reason: Both identify the same electrochemical quantity; the proposed enhancement mechanisms and assertion strengths belong to the claims.

clusters.label: Ionic conductivity
clusters.definition: Electrical conductivity attributable to mobile ions.
clusters.reason: All denote ionic charge conductivity, distinct from electronic and thermal conductivity. Materials, ionic species, conditions, enhancement or suppression, and negation remain claim attributes; no endpoint specifically denotes an interface conductivity or a conductivity change.

clusters.label: Ionic conductivity (lattice gas model)
clusters.definition: Ionic charge conductivity predicted using a lattice gas model of mobile ions.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly concern model-derived conductivity. Their different concentration variables and mobile-ion populations remain attached to their respective predictions.

clusters.label: Ionic thermoelectric performance (gel thermocells)
clusters.definition: Heat-to-electric conversion performance of ionic gel thermocells involving redox exchange.
clusters.reason: Both contexts explicitly connect thermocell performance with exchange current density and ionic transport.

clusters.label: Ionic thermoelectric performance (cement-based composites)
clusters.definition: Ionic thermoelectric conversion performance of cement-based composites.
clusters.reason: Both denote the stated performance class in cement-based composites, with pore structure affecting that performance; they do not identify a shared sample.

clusters.label: Ionic thermoelectric performance (simulated nanochannels)
clusters.definition: Predicted thermoelectric performance of ionic transport in nanochannels with hydrodynamic slippage.
clusters.reason: Explicitly concerns a numerical nanochannel model and thermoosmosis-enhanced short-circuit current, preserving its predictive status and mechanism.

clusters.label: Low-grade heat harvesting
clusters.definition: Recovery of low-grade thermal energy as useful electrical energy.
clusters.reason: All denote the same application. Conversion mechanisms, device compositions, demonstrated operation, and proposed potential remain distinct claims.

clusters.label: Ionic thermopower
clusters.definition: Thermally generated voltage per temperature difference associated with ionic redistribution.
clusters.reason: The evidence consistently identifies ionic thermopower, with explicit mobility asymmetry or Soret redistribution where mechanisms are supplied. Compositions and enhancement mechanisms remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Ionic thermopower (gel thermocell)
clusters.definition: Thermopower identified as ionic in a graphene-containing gel thermocell.
clusters.reason: The thermocell context does not establish equivalence with the Soret-based thermopower endpoints; its redox-associated context is preserved.

clusters.label: Ionic thermopower (negative)
clusters.definition: Negative ionic thermopower of the cellulose-nanofibril-containing PAM hydrogel.
clusters.reason: The supplied title explicitly specifies a high negative Seebeck coefficient, warranting preservation of direction.

clusters.label: Ionic thermopower (mixed-conductor model)
clusters.definition: The ionic thermopower contribution analyzed through the thermodynamic factor in a four-carrier model of mixed-conducting BaTiO3.
clusters.reason: Explicitly a theoretical ionic contribution involving mobile oxide ions and hole trapping, distinguished from the model's electronic thermopower.

clusters.label: Reusability
clusters.definition: Capacity for repeated use while retaining functional performance.
clusters.reason: Both describe retained usability over time. Thermoelectric properties and electromyographic signal quality are different supporting performance measures.

unresolved.reason: “Good mechanical properties” does not specify a mechanical quantity, behavior, or criterion sufficient to determine equivalence.
The evidence supplies no particular mechanical property or criterion defining the generic favorable assessment.

clusters.label: Self-healing
clusters.definition: Capacity of a material or device to recover integrity or function after damage.
clusters.reason: All endpoints denote the recovery capability. Water assistance, noncovalent interactions, structural support, encapsulation, and material compositions describe individual implementations rather than equivalent healing mechanisms.

clusters.label: Thermoelectric conversion efficiency
clusters.definition: Efficiency with which thermal input is converted into electrical output through thermoelectric operation.
clusters.reason: All identify conversion efficiency as the outcome. Materials, transport and electrode mechanisms, treatments, and proposed improvements remain attached to individual claims; none denotes the efficiency increase itself.
